findings.F1: Step 5's main measure is on the side the idea predicts but below the bar: the mean unusual 8-day move in the short direction is +0.84 % per case (t 1.44, 436 cases, strength 0.048), and my own case reading gives +1.05 % (t 1.89, 486 cases), also short of t 2.
findings.F2: The effect only appears beyond a few days and grows with time: the mean unusual short move is -0.01 % at 2 days (t -0.05, 513 cases), +0.12 % at 4 days (t 0.29, 502), +1.05 % at 8 days (t 1.89, 486) and +2.12 % at 16 days (t 2.40, 445).
findings.F3: The effect sits in coins already falling over 60 days: with a negative 60-day return, cases move +1.70 % over 8 days (t 2.61, 320 cases) and +2.80 % over 16 days (t 2.99, 311). With a positive 60-day return they move -0.21 % (t -0.21, 166) and +0.52 % (t 0.26, 134).
findings.F4: The effect is mixed across years: 2018 gives +8.28 % (t 4.33, 39 cases), 2023 +1.84 % (t 2.33, 68) and 2020 -3.03 % (t -2.57, 80); every other year has |t| below 1.2.
findings.F5: The effect is mixed across coins at 8 days: XRP +2.71 % (t 2.04, 61 cases), ZEC +3.23 % (t 1.76, 75) and BTC +1.54 % (t 1.69, 92), while LTC is -0.94 % (t -0.57, 83) and XMR -0.19 % (t -0.19, 94). Six coins leave each with under 100 cases.
findings.F6: The grading by depth holds only past the shallowest failures: the lowest depth tercile gives -0.49 % (t -0.50, 163 cases), the middle +1.96 % (t 2.24, 162) and the deepest +1.68 % (t 1.66, 161). The slope of the move on |forecast| is +0.0027 (t 1.69, 486 cases).
findings.F7: The market's own rise cancels the effect on the book: the coins' normal drift is -1.05 % per case in the short direction. That leaves a total move of -0.21 %, against a 0.19 % cost per trade. The total short move is about zero at every horizon (8 days: -0.004 %, t -0.01), and the book's Sharpe is -0.14.

ideas.name: failed breakout, more coins
ideas.idea: After a close back below the old 20-day high within 3 days of a breakout above it, the coin's decline continues across the following 8 days only while its close 2 days after the failure is still below that old high. The further that day-2 close sits below the old high, the larger the fall from day 2 to day 10.
ideas.consequence: A trader would short a failed breakout only once price has stayed below the old high for two days, sized by the current distance below it, and would refuse the short when price is already back above.

ideas.idea: After a close back below the old 20-day high within 3 days of a breakout above it, the coin's decline continues while its close 2 days after the failure is still below that old high, only while the coin's 60-day return is negative. The further that day-2 close sits below the old high, the larger the fall over the next 16 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would short a failed breakout that stays below the old high only in a coin already falling over 60 days, hold it about two weeks and size it by the depth below the old high, and would refuse it in a coin rising over 60 days.
ideas.name: failed breakout in downtrends
